title: Who Is the Author of a Film?
objective: After this level you can weigh the auteur theory, which credits the director, against the view of film as a team effort.
summary: The auteur theory treats the director as a film's author; Kael argued Citizen Kane was a collaboration, and Toland's role supports the team view.

cards.headline: Who made Citizen Kane?
cards.body: The credits say Orson Welles directed, produced, starred, and co-wrote it with Herman J. Mankiewicz. In 1971 critic Pauline Kael challenged Welles's role as its author and named Mankiewicz its main creative force. So whose film is it?

cards.headline: The auteur theory: the director as author
cards.body: The auteur theory sees the director, who oversees every sound and image, as a film's major creative force, more its author than the screenwriter. The idea grew in France in the late 1940s and was advanced through Cahiers du cinéma, founded in 1951: the magazine where Level 62's Truffaut and Godard wrote as critics. American critic Andrew Sarris named it the auteur theory in a 1962 essay.

cards.headline: The case for a team
cards.body: Kael's essay "Raising Kane" (1971) argued that Kane wasn't simply Welles's: she named co-writer Herman J. Mankiewicz its main creative force. Sarris and Peter Bogdanovich were among her notable opponents, questioning both her argument and her facts. The fight is still a good one, because both sides can point at the screen.

cards.headline: Evidence you can weigh
cards.body: Welles later admitted that his cinematographer, Gregg Toland, advised him on lighting effects and camera placement. That's the man behind Kane's deep focus. Yet a director can also be the one who chooses such collaborators and shapes their work into one style. The honest answer may be both.

mascot.line: Keep this: 'auteur or team?' is a question to weigh with evidence, not a side to pick.

cards.headline: Who Is the Author of a Film?: done
learned: Auteur theory: the director as author
It grew from Cahiers du cinéma; Sarris named it
Kael argued Kane was a collaboration
Weigh the evidence: often it's both

questions.prompt: The auteur theory treats _____ as the author of a film.

options.label: the screenwriter
options.rationale: The theory ranks the director above the screenwriter.

options.label: the studio that paid for it
options.rationale: The studio era is Chapter 5; the theory credits the director.

options.label: the audience
options.rationale: The theory is about who creates the film.

questions.explanation: The auteur theory sees the director, who oversees sound and image, as the film's major creative force.

questions.prompt: Which piece of evidence best supports the view that Citizen Kane was a team effort?

options.label: Welles appears in the film
options.rationale: Acting in it doesn't show others shaped it.

options.label: Cahiers du cinéma was founded in 1951
options.rationale: That's about the theory's origin, not Kane's making.

options.label: Welles admitted Toland advised him on lighting and camera placement
Sarris named the auteur theory in 1962
options.rationale: That supports the idea's history, not the team view.

questions.explanation: Toland's advice on lighting and camera placement shows key choices came from a collaborator.

questions.prompt: The auteur theory was advanced through Cahiers du cinéma. Who from Level 62 wrote for it as critics before directing?

options.label: Satyajit Ray and Yasujirō Ozu
options.rationale: They weren't Cahiers critics in this tree.

options.label: Orson Welles and Gregg Toland
options.rationale: They made Citizen Kane in Hollywood.

questions.explanation: Truffaut and Godard wrote for Cahiers du cinéma in the 1950s, then led the New Wave as directors.
